test_title: PYST 03: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

A blog page has been created by the head of the department for the conference.

options.text: The head of the department has been creating a blog page for the conference.
The head of the department has created a blog page for the conference.
The head of the department was creating a blog page for the conference.
The head of the department created a blog page for the conference.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the given passive voice sentence: "A blog page has been created by the head of the department for the conference."
 
• To convert it into active voice, place the original subject ("the head of the department") at the beginning.
 
• Change the verb "has been created" to "has created" to maintain the present perfect tense.
 
• Ensure that the object ("a blog page") and the phrase "for the conference" remain in place.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The head of the department has created a blog page for the conference."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The head of the department has been creating a blog page for the conference." – Incorrect as it changes the meaning by implying an ongoing action.
 
• **Option 3: **"The head of the department was creating a blog page for the conference." – Incorrect as it changes the tense to past continuous.
 
• **Option 4: **"The head of the department created a blog page for the conference." – Incorrect as it changes the tense to simple past.
